scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

content.description: The step, as a short imperative phrase (≤7 words).

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list. Use on the first call and whenever the plan changes.

advance.description: true: the in_progress step is done and the next pending step starts (the cheap, usual update).

done.description: 1-based numbers of steps just completed (out-of-order updates).

start.description: 1-based number of the step now in progress (with done, for out-of-order updates).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
schema.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__find

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

## context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. """Plain inputs of the portfolio overview, loaded once per request.

Every entity attribute is read inside the session and copied into frozen
dataclasses, so the calculations in ``resource_path`` and ``portfolio`` stay
pure and testable without a database.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from datetime import date, timedelta

from alloq_commons.entities.employee import EmployeeEntity
from alloq_commons.entities.project import ProjectEntity
from alloq_commons.entities.risk import RiskEntity
from alloq_commons.entities.role import RoleEntity
from alloq_commons.models.employee import STANDARD_WEEKLY_HOURS
from alloq_commons.repositories import (
    employee_repo,
    project_repo,
    public_holiday_repo,
    risk_repo,
)
from alloq_commons.repositories.risk_repository import MAX_RISK_IMPACT, MIN_RISK_IMPACT
from sqlalchemy import select

from appkit_commons.database.session import get_asyncdb_session

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SCOPE_DEPARTMENT = "department"
SCOPE_TEAM = "team"
SCOPES = (SCOPE_DEPARTMENT, SCOPE_TEAM)
LOOKAHEAD_WEEKS = 52
MAX_ROWS = 1000


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AllocationInput:
    employee_id: int
    role_id: int
    week_start: date
    person_days: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProjectInput:
    id: int
    code: str
    name: str
    state: str
    start_date: date
    end_date: date
    budget: int
    progress: int = 0
    eac: float = 0.0
    owner_ids: tuple[int, ...] = ()
    required: tuple[tuple[int, float], ...] = ()
    allocations: tuple[AllocationInput, ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EmployeeInput:
    id: int
    name: str
    role_ids: tuple[int, ...] = ()
    manager_id: int | None = None
    internal_hours: int = 0
    workload_percent: int = 100
    absences: tuple[tuple[date, date], ...] = ()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RoleInput:
    id: int
    name: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RiskInput:
    id: int
    project_id: int
    name: str
    probability: int
    impact: int
    mitigation_status: str = "open"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PortfolioInputs:
    """Everything the portfolio needs.

    ``projects`` and ``employees`` are the scope shown; ``all_projects`` and
    ``all_employees`` stay complete, because bookings on any project use up a
    person's time.
    """

    projects: tuple[ProjectInput, ...] = ()
    all_projects: tuple[ProjectInput, ...] = ()
    employees: tuple[EmployeeInput, ...] = ()
    all_employees: tuple[EmployeeInput, ...] = ()
    roles: tuple[RoleInput, ...] = ()
    risks: tuple[RiskInput, ...] = ()
    holidays: frozenset[date] = frozenset()
    current_employee_id: int | None = None


def clamp(value: int, low: int, high: int) -> int:
    return max(low, min(high, value))


def team_employee_ids(inputs: PortfolioInputs) -> set[int]:
    """Direct reports of the signed-in employee."""
    manager = inputs.current_employee_id
    if manager is None:
        return set()
    return {e.id for e in inputs.all_employees if e.manager_id == manager}


def booking_projects(inputs: PortfolioInputs) -> tuple[ProjectInput, ...]:
    return inputs.all_projects or inputs.projects


def apply_scope(inputs: PortfolioInputs, scope: str) -> PortfolioInputs:
    """Restrict people to direct reports and projects to owned ones."""
    if scope != SCOPE_TEAM:
        return inputs
    manager = inputs.current_employee_id
    team = team_employee_ids(inputs)
    return replace(
        inputs,
        employees=tuple(e for e in inputs.all_employees if e.id in team),
        projects=tuple(
            p
            for p in booking_projects(inputs)
            if manager is not None and manager in p.owner_ids
        ),
    )


def _latest_eac(entity: ProjectEntity) -> float:
    """EAC from the project, else from its newest status snapshot."""
    if entity.ev_eac_additive:
        return float(entity.ev_eac_additive)
    latest = entity.statuses[0] if entity.statuses else None
    if latest is None:
        return 0.0
    for value in (latest.eac_additive, latest.eac_linear):
        if value:
            return float(value)
    budget = float(entity.budget or 0)
    spent = (
        float(latest.actual_cost)
        if latest.actual_cost
        else budget * (latest.budget_spent or 0) / 100.0
    )
    if spent > 0 and latest.progress:
        return spent / (latest.progress / 100.0)
    return 0.0


def project_to_input(entity: ProjectEntity) -> ProjectInput:
    latest = entity.statuses[0] if entity.statuses else None
    required: dict[int, float] = {}
    for rc in entity.required_capacities or []:
        required[rc.role_id] = required.get(rc.role_id, 0.0) + float(rc.person_days)
    return ProjectInput(
        id=entity.id,
        code=entity.code,
        name=entity.name_de,
        state=entity.state,
        start_date=entity.start_date,
        end_date=entity.end_date,
        budget=entity.budget or 0,
        progress=latest.progress if latest else 0,
        eac=_latest_eac(entity),
        owner_ids=tuple(o.id for o in entity.owners or []),
        required=tuple(sorted(required.items())),
        allocations=tuple(
            AllocationInput(
                employee_id=a.employee_id,
                role_id=a.role_id,
                week_start=a.week_start,
                person_days=float(a.person_days),
            )
            for a in entity.capacity_allocations or []
        ),
    )


def employee_to_input(entity: EmployeeEntity) -> EmployeeInput:
    return EmployeeInput(
        id=entity.id,
        name=f"{entity.first_name} {entity.last_name}".strip(),
        role_ids=tuple(r.id for r in entity.roles or []),
        manager_id=entity.manager_id,
        internal_hours=int(entity.internal_hours or 0),
        workload_percent=round(
            float(entity.hours_per_week or STANDARD_WEEKLY_HOURS)
            / STANDARD_WEEKLY_HOURS
            * 100
        ),
        absences=tuple(
            (a.start_date, a.end_date)
            for a in entity.absences or []
            if a.start_date and a.end_date
        ),
    )


def risk_to_input(entity: RiskEntity) -> RiskInput:
    return RiskInput(
        id=entity.id,
        project_id=entity.project_id,
        name=entity.name,
        probability=clamp(entity.probability, MIN_RISK_IMPACT, MAX_RISK_IMPACT),
        impact=clamp(entity.impact, MIN_RISK_IMPACT, MAX_RISK_IMPACT),
        mitigation_status=entity.mitigation_status,
    )


async def load_inputs(today: date, email: str | None) -> PortfolioInputs:
    """Load projects, people, roles, open risks and holidays."""
    monday = today - timedelta(days=today.weekday())
    async with get_asyncdb_session() as session:
        projects = await project_repo.find_all_paginated(session, limit=MAX_ROWS)
        project_rows = tuple(project_to_input(p) for p in projects)
        employees = await employee_repo.find_all_paginated(session, limit=MAX_ROWS)
        employee_rows = tuple(employee_to_input(e) for e in employees)
        result = await session.execute(select(RoleEntity).order_by(RoleEntity.name))
        role_rows = tuple(RoleInput(id=r.id, name=r.name) for r in result.scalars())
        risks = await risk_repo.find_open_by_min_score(session, min_score=0)
        risk_rows = tuple(risk_to_input(r) for r in risks)
        holidays = await public_holiday_repo.find_by_date_range(
            session, monday, monday + timedelta(weeks=LOOKAHEAD_WEEKS)
        )
        holiday_dates = frozenset(h.date for h in holidays if h.date)
        current = await employee_repo.find_by_email(session, email) if email else None
        current_id = current.id if current else None
    logger.debug(
        "Portfolio inputs: %d projects, %d employees, %d risks",
        len(project_rows),
        len(employee_rows),
        len(risk_rows),
    )
    return PortfolioInputs(
        projects=project_rows,
        all_projects=project_rows,
        employees=employee_rows,
        all_employees=employee_rows,
        roles=role_rows,
        risks=risk_rows,
        holidays=holiday_dates,
        current_employee_id=current_id,
    )
"""State of the portfolio overview (dashboard variant C)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from typing import Any

import reflex as rx

from alloq_dashboard.models import PortfolioKpi, PortfolioProject, RiskItem
from alloq_dashboard.services import portfolio
from alloq_dashboard.services.portfolio_inputs import SCOPE_DEPARTMENT, SCOPES
from appkit_user.authentication.decorators import requires_admin
from appkit_user.authentication.states import LoginState, UserSession

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

LOAD_ERROR_MESSAGE = "Daten konnten nicht geladen werden."
DRAWER_PROJECT = "project"
DRAWER_RISKS = "risks"


class PortfolioState(UserSession):
    """Portfolio payload, the chosen scope and the open drawer."""

    data: rx.Field[PortfolioKpi] = rx.field(default_factory=PortfolioKpi)
    is_loading: rx.Field[bool] = rx.field(False)
    error_message: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    scope: rx.Field[str] = rx.field(SCOPE_DEPARTMENT)
    drawer: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    selected_project_id: rx.Field[int] = rx.field(0)
    selected_cell: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")

    @rx.var
    def selected_project(self) -> PortfolioProject:
        return next(
            (p for p in self.data.projects if p.id == self.selected_project_id),
            PortfolioProject(),
        )

    @rx.var
    def cell_risks(self) -> list[RiskItem]:
        return [
            r
            for r in self.data.risks
            if f"{r.probability}-{r.impact}" == self.selected_cell
        ]

    @rx.var
    def cell_title(self) -> str:
        if not self.selected_cell:
            return ""
        probability, impact = self.selected_cell.split("-")
        return f"Wahrscheinlichkeit {probability}, Auswirkung {impact}"

    async def _user_email(self) -> str | None:
        login_state = await self.get_state(LoginState)
        user = await login_state.authenticated_user
        return getattr(user, "email", None) if user else None

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def load(self) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        """Load the portfolio for the current scope."""
        self.is_loading = True
        self.error_message = ""
        yield
        try:
            email = await self._user_email()
            self.data = await portfolio.load_portfolio(self.scope, email)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Portfolio load failed")
            self.error_message = LOAD_ERROR_MESSAGE
        finally:
            self.is_loading = False

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def set_scope(self, scope: str) -> Any:
        """Switch between the whole department and direct reports."""
        if scope not in SCOPES or scope == self.scope:
            return None
        self.scope = scope
        self.drawer = ""
        return PortfolioState.load

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def open_project(self, project_id: int) -> None:
        self.selected_project_id = project_id
        self.drawer = DRAWER_PROJECT

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def open_risk_cell(self, key: str) -> None:
        self.selected_cell = key
        self.drawer = DRAWER_RISKS

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def close_drawer(self) -> None:
        self.drawer = ""

    """

    projects: tuple[ProjectInput, ...] = ()
    all_projects: tuple[ProjectInput, ...] = ()
    employees: tuple[EmployeeInput, ...] = ()
    all_employees: tuple[EmployeeInput, ...] = ()
    roles: tuple[RoleInput, ...] = ()
    risks: tuple[RiskInput, ...] = ()
    holidays: frozenset[date] = frozenset()
    current_employee_id: int | None = None


def clamp(value: int, low: int, high: int) -> int:
    return max(low, min(high, value))


def team_employee_ids(inputs: PortfolioInputs) -> set[int]:
    """Direct reports of the signed-in employee."""
    manager = inputs.current_employee_id
    if manager is None:
        return set()
    return {e.id for e in inputs.all_employees if e.manager_id == manager}


def booking_projects(inputs: PortfolioInputs) -> tuple[ProjectInput, ...]:
    return inputs.all_projects or inputs.projects


def apply_scope(inputs: PortfolioInputs, scope: str) -> PortfolioInputs:
    """Restrict people to direct reports and projects to owned ones."""
    if scope != SCOPE_TEAM:
        return inputs
    manager = inputs.current_employee_id
    team = team_employee_ids(inputs)
    return replace(
        inputs,
        employees=tuple(e for e in inputs.all_employees if e.id in team),
        projects=tuple(
            p
            for p in booking_projects(inputs)
            if manager is not None and manager in p.owner_ids
        ),
    )


def _latest_eac(entity: ProjectEntity) -> float:
    """EAC from the project, else from its newest status snapshot."""
    if entity.ev_eac_additive:
        return float(entity.ev_eac_additive)
    latest = entity.statuses[0] if entity.statuses else None
    if latest is None:
        return 0.0
    for value in (latest.eac_additive, latest.eac_linear):
        if value:
            return float(value)
    budget = float(entity.budget or 0)
    spent = (
        float(latest.actual_cost)
        if latest.actual_cost
        else budget * (latest.budget_spent or 0) / 100.0
    )
    if spent > 0 and latest.progress:
        return spent / (latest.progress / 100.0)
    return 0.0


def project_to_input(entity: ProjectEntity) -> ProjectInput:
    latest = entity.statuses[0] if entity.statuses else None
    required: dict[int, float] = {}
    for rc in entity.required_capacities or []:
        required[rc.role_id] = required.get(rc.role_id, 0.0) + float(rc.person_days)
    return ProjectInput(
        id=entity.id,
        code=entity.code,
        name=entity.name_de,
        state=entity.state,
        start_date=entity.start_date,
        end_date=entity.end_date,
        budget=entity.budget or 0,
        progress=latest.progress if latest else 0,
        eac=_latest_eac(entity),
        owner_ids=tuple(o.id for o in entity.owners or []),
        required=tuple(sorted(required.items())),
        allocations=tuple(
            AllocationInput(
                employee_id=a.employee_id,
                role_id=a.role_id,
                week_start=a.week_start,
                person_days=float(a.person_days),
            )
            for a in entity.capacity_allocations or []
        ),
    )


def employee_to_input(entity: EmployeeEntity) -> EmployeeInput:
    return EmployeeInput(
        id=entity.id,
        name=f"{entity.first_name} {entity.last_name}".strip(),
        role_ids=tuple(r.id for r in entity.roles or []),
        manager_id=entity.manager_id,
        internal_hours=int(entity.internal_hours or 0),
        workload_percent=round(
            float(entity.hours_per_week or STANDARD_WEEKLY_HOURS)
            / STANDARD_WEEKLY_HOURS
            * 100
        ),
        absences=tuple(
            (a.start_date, a.end_date)
            for a in entity.absences or []
            if a.start_date and a.end_date
        ),
    )


def risk_to_input(entity: RiskEntity) -> RiskInput:
    return RiskInput(
        id=entity.id,
        project_id=entity.project_id,
        name=entity.name,
        probability=clamp(entity.probability, MIN_RISK_IMPACT, MAX_RISK_IMPACT),
        impact=clamp(entity.impact, MIN_RISK_IMPACT, MAX_RISK_IMPACT),
        mitigation_status=entity.mitigation_status,
    )


async def load_inputs(today: date, email: str | None) -> PortfolioInputs:
    """Load projects, people, roles, open risks and holidays."""
    monday = today - timedelta(days=today.weekday())
    async with get_asyncdb_session() as session:
        projects = await project_repo.find_all_paginated(session, limit=MAX_ROWS)
        project_rows = tuple(project_to_input(p) for p in projects)
        employees = await employee_repo.find_all_paginated(session, limit=MAX_ROWS)
        employee_rows = tuple(employee_to_input(e) for e in employees)
        result = await session.execute(select(RoleEntity).order_by(RoleEntity.name))
        role_rows = tuple(RoleInput(id=r.id, name=r.name) for r in result.scalars())
        risks = await risk_repo.find_open_by_min_score(session, min_score=0)
        risk_rows = tuple(risk_to_input(r) for r in risks)
        holidays = await public_holiday_repo.find_by_date_range(
            session, monday, monday + timedelta(weeks=LOOKAHEAD_WEEKS)
        )
        holiday_dates = frozenset(h.date for h in holidays if h.date)
        current = await employee_repo.find_by_email(session, email) if email else None
        current_id = current.id if current else None
    logger.debug(
        "Portfolio inputs: %d projects, %d employees, %d risks",
        len(project_rows),
        len(employee_rows),
        len(risk_rows),
    )
    return PortfolioInputs(
        projects=project_rows,
        all_projects=project_rows,
        employees=employee_rows,
        all_employees=employee_rows,
        roles=role_rows,
        risks=risk_rows,
        holidays=holiday_dates,
        current_employee_id=current_id,
    )

class PortfolioState(UserSession):
    """Portfolio payload, the chosen scope and the open drawer."""

    data: rx.Field[PortfolioKpi] = rx.field(default_factory=PortfolioKpi)
    is_loading: rx.Field[bool] = rx.field(False)
    error_message: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    scope: rx.Field[str] = rx.field(SCOPE_DEPARTMENT)
    drawer: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")
    selected_project_id: rx.Field[int] = rx.field(0)
    selected_cell: rx.Field[str] = rx.field("")

    @rx.var
    def selected_project(self) -> PortfolioProject:
        return next(
            (p for p in self.data.projects if p.id == self.selected_project_id),
            PortfolioProject(),
        )

    @rx.var
    def cell_risks(self) -> list[RiskItem]:
        return [
            r
            for r in self.data.risks
            if f"{r.probability}-{r.impact}" == self.selected_cell
        ]

    @rx.var
    def cell_title(self) -> str:
        if not self.selected_cell:
            return ""
        probability, impact = self.selected_cell.split("-")
        return f"Wahrscheinlichkeit {probability}, Auswirkung {impact}"

    async def _user_email(self) -> str | None:
        login_state = await self.get_state(LoginState)
        user = await login_state.authenticated_user
        return getattr(user, "email", None) if user else None

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def load(self) -> AsyncGenerator[Any]:
        """Load the portfolio for the current scope."""
        self.is_loading = True
        self.error_message = ""
        yield
        try:
            email = await self._user_email()
            self.data = await portfolio.load_portfolio(self.scope, email)
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Portfolio load failed")
            self.error_message = LOAD_ERROR_MESSAGE
        finally:
            self.is_loading = False

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def set_scope(self, scope: str) -> Any:
        """Switch between the whole department and direct reports."""
        if scope not in SCOPES or scope == self.scope:
            return None
        self.scope = scope
        self.drawer = ""
        return PortfolioState.load

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def open_project(self, project_id: int) -> None:
        self.selected_project_id = project_id
        self.drawer = DRAWER_PROJECT

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def open_risk_cell(self, key: str) -> None:
        self.selected_cell = key
        self.drawer = DRAWER_RISKS

    @rx.event
    @requires_admin
    async def close_drawer(self) -> None:
        self.drawer = ""

def _fact(label: str, value: rx.Component) -> rx.Component:

def card(
    title: str,
    subtitle: str | rx.Var[str],
    body: rx.Component,
    *,
    is_loading: rx.Var[bool],
    aside: rx.Component | None = None,
    label: str = "",
) -> rx.Component:
    """White card with a title, one line of context and a loading skeleton."""
    header = mn.group(
        mn.stack(
            mn.text(title, fz="14px", fw=650, c=theme.TEXT),

        gap="md",
    )
    skeleton = mn.stack(
        mn.skeleton(height="14px", width="60%"),
        mn.skeleton(height="14px", width="80%"),
        mn.skeleton(height="14px", width="40%"),
        gap="sm",
        pt="md",

    return mn.box(
        mn.stack(
            header,
            rx.cond(is_loading, skeleton, body),
            gap="sm",
            h="100%",

        style={**theme.CARD, "padding": "14px 16px", "minWidth": "0"},
        custom_attrs={"role": "region", "aria-label": label or title},

"""Tests for PortfolioState: load, scope switch and drawer."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Any
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch

import pytest
from alloq_dashboard.models import PortfolioKpi, PortfolioProject, RiskItem
from alloq_dashboard.states.portfolio_state import (
    DRAWER_PROJECT,
    DRAWER_RISKS,
    LOAD_ERROR_MESSAGE,
    PortfolioState,
)

from appkit_user.authentication.backend.models import User

LOADER = "alloq_dashboard.states.portfolio_state.portfolio.load_portfolio"
ADMIN = User(user_id=1, name="Katrin", email="katrin@example.com", is_admin=True)
MEMBER = User(user_id=2, name="Ben", is_admin=False)


class _FakeLogin:
    def __init__(self, user: User | None) -> None:
        self._user = user

    @property
    def authenticated_user(self) -> Any:
        async def _get() -> User | None:
            return self._user

        return _get()

    async def redir(self) -> None:
        return None


def _login(user: User | None) -> Any:
    return patch.object(
        PortfolioState, "get_state", new=AsyncMock(return_value=_FakeLogin(user))
    )


@pytest.fixture
def as_admin() -> Iterator[None]:
    with _login(ADMIN):
        yield


async def _drain(handler: Any, state: PortfolioState, *args: Any) -> list[Any]:
    fn = handler.fn
    result = fn(state, *args)
    if hasattr(result, "__aiter__"):
        return [item async for item in result]
    return [await result]


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("as_admin")
async def test_load_stores_payload_for_scope_and_email() -> None:
    state = PortfolioState()
    state.scope = "team"
    loader = AsyncMock(return_value=PortfolioKpi(scope="team", gap_total=12.0))
    with patch(LOADER, new=loader):
        await _drain(PortfolioState.load, state)

    loader.assert_awaited_once_with("team", "katrin@example.com")
    assert state.data.gap_total == 12.0
    assert state.is_loading is False
    assert state.error_message == ""


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("as_admin")
async def test_load_failure_shows_message() -> None:
    state = PortfolioState()
    with patch(LOADER, new=AsyncMock(side_effect=RuntimeError("db down"))):
        await _drain(PortfolioState.load, state)

    assert state.is_loading is False
    assert state.error_message == LOAD_ERROR_MESSAGE


async def test_load_is_refused_for_non_admins() -> None:
    state = PortfolioState()
    loader = AsyncMock()
    with _login(MEMBER), patch(LOADER, new=loader):
        await _drain(PortfolioState.load, state)
    loader.assert_not_awaited()


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("as_admin")
async def test_set_scope_reloads_only_on_change() -> None:
    state = PortfolioState()
    state.drawer = DRAWER_PROJECT

    assert await _drain(PortfolioState.set_scope, state, "team") == [
        PortfolioState.load
    ]
    assert state.scope == "team"
    assert state.drawer == ""
    assert await _drain(PortfolioState.set_scope, state, "team") == [None]
    assert await _drain(PortfolioState.set_scope, state, "everyone") == [None]
    assert state.scope == "team"


@pytest.mark.usefixtures("as_admin")
async def test_drawer_selection_and_computed_vars() -> None:
    state = PortfolioState()
    state.data = PortfolioKpi(
        projects=[PortfolioProject(id=4, code="AQ-104")],
        risks=[
            RiskItem(id=1, name="A", probability=4, impact=5),
            RiskItem(id=2, name="B", probability=3, impact=3),
        ],
    )
    assert state.cell_title == ""

    await _drain(PortfolioState.open_project, state, 4)
    assert state.drawer == DRAWER_PROJECT
    assert state.selected_project.code == "AQ-104"

    await _drain(PortfolioState.open_risk_cell, state, "4-5")
    assert state.drawer == DRAWER_RISKS
    assert [r.id for r in state.cell_risks] == [1]
    assert state.cell_title == "Wahrscheinlichkeit 4, Auswirkung 5"

    await _drain(PortfolioState.close_drawer, state)
    assert state.drawer == ""
    state.selected_project_id = 99
    assert state.selected_project.code == ""

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Capacity
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_free_capacity_is_not_clamped_when_overbooked() -> None:
    p = project(1, "P1", end=friday(4), allocations=(alloc(1, 0, 7),))
    capacity = Capacity(inputs((p,), (emp(1, "A"),)), Calendar.for_today(TODAY))

    assert capacity.free(BACKEND, 0) == pytest.approx(-2.0)
    assert capacity.free(BACKEND, 1) == pytest.approx(5.0)
    assert capacity.percent(1) == 140
    assert capacity.percent(99) is None


def test_bookings_in_other_roles_reduce_role_availability() -> None:
    p = project(1, "P1", end=friday(4), allocations=(alloc(1, 0, 3, role=QA),))
    capacity = Capacity(
        inputs((p,), (emp(1, "A", roles=(BACKEND, QA)),)), Calendar.for_today(TODAY)
    )
    assert capacity.role_available[BACKEND][0] == pytest.approx(2.0)
    assert capacity.free(QA, 0) == pytest.approx(2.0)


def test_completed_projects_do_not_book_capacity() -> None:
    done = project(
        1,
        "P1",
        end=friday(4),
        state=ProjectStateEnum.COMPLETED.value,
        allocations=(alloc(1, 0, 5),),
    )
    capacity = Capacity(inputs((done,), (emp(1, "A"),)), Calendar.for_today(TODAY))
    assert capacity.free(BACKEND, 0) == pytest.approx(5.0)

# Buffer and weakest link

def test_planned_work_sets_the_cover_week() -> None:
    # Required 12, 2 already booked last week, the remaining 10 planned.
    p = project(
        1,
        "P1",
        end=friday(5),
        required=((BACKEND, 12),),
        allocations=(alloc(1, -1, 2), alloc(1, 0, 5), alloc(1, 1, 5)),
    )
    line = lines_for(inputs((p,), (emp(1, "Anna"), emp(2, "Ben"))))[1][0]

    assert line.remaining_days == 10
    assert line.planned_days == 10
    assert line.gap_days == 0
    assert line.buffer_weeks == 4
    assert line.tone == "warn"
    assert line.reason == "Einzige Person für die Rolle."
    assert line.person_label == "Anna"


def test_gap_without_carrier_gives_negative_buffer() -> None:
    # 30 PT gap, one free person with 5 PT a week: covered in week 5, ends week 2.
    p = project(1, "P1", end=friday(2), required=((BACKEND, 30),))
    line = lines_for(inputs((p,), (emp(1, "A"),)))[1][0]

    assert line.gap_days == 30
    assert line.buffer_weeks == -3
    assert line.person_label == "niemand eingeplant"
    assert line.tone == "neg"
    assert line.reason == "30 PT ohne Plan."


def test_uncovered_gap_is_flagged() -> None:
    p = project(1, "P1", end=friday(2), required=((QA, 10),))
    line = lines_for(inputs((p,), (emp(1, "A"),)))[1][0]

    assert line.covered is False
    assert line.tone == "neg"
    assert line.reason.startswith("Nicht gedeckt in 52 Wochen.")


def test_overbooked_role_is_named_with_its_first_week() -> None:
    p = project(
        1,
        "P1",
        end=friday(6),
        required=((BACKEND, 20),),
        allocations=(alloc(1, 2, 7),),
    )
    line = lines_for(inputs((p,), (emp(1, "A"),)))[1][0]

    assert line.tone == "neg"
    assert line.reason == "Rolle ab KW 44 überbucht. 13 PT ohne Plan."


def test_single_absent_carrier_is_a_warning() -> None:
    carrier = emp(1, "Mira", absences=((week(2), friday(3)),))
    p = project(
        1,
        "P1",
        end=friday(8),
        required=((BACKEND, 4),),
        allocations=(alloc(1, 0, 4),),

    assert line.tone == "warn"
    assert line.reason == "Einzige Person für die Rolle. Abwesend KW 44 bis KW 45."


def test_overloaded_carrier_near_the_end() -> None:
    p = project(

    assert line.tone == "neg"
    assert line.person_label == "Jonas"
    assert line.reason == "120 % ausgelastet. Das Projekt endet am 06.11."


def test_several_carriers_with_gap_and_covered() -> None:

    team = (
        emp(1, "Katrin", roles=()),

    )
    late = project(
        1,

    )

    risks = (

        RiskInput(2, 1, "Team überbucht", 5, 4),

        RiskInput(4, 2, "Akzeptanz", 1, 2),
        RiskInput(5, 2, "Erledigt", 3, 3, mitigation_status="resolved"),
    )
    return inputs((late, calm, planned, done), team, risks=risks, current=1)


def test_build_portfolio_for_the_department() -> None:
    kpi = portfolio.build_portfolio(_sample(), SCOPE_DEPARTMENT, TODAY)

    assert kpi.scope == "department"
    assert kpi.notice == ""
    assert kpi.department_employee_count == 3
    assert kpi.team_employee_count == 2
    assert [p.code for p in kpi.projects] == ["AQ-104", "AQ-112", "AQ-118"]
    late = kpi.projects[0]
    assert late.health == "red"
    assert late.eac_delta_percent == 12.5
    assert late.buffer_label == "\u22123"
    assert late.weakest.role_name == "Backend"

    assert [b.code for b in kpi.bubbles] == ["AQ-104", "AQ-112"]
    assert kpi.bubbles[0].negative_buffer is True
    assert kpi.bubbles[0].size == "60px"
    assert kpi.bubbles[0].top == "calc(59% - 30.0px)"
    assert kpi.bubbles[0].label_top == "calc(59% - 8px)"
    assert "Budget 720.000 €" in kpi.bubbles[0].tooltip
    assert kpi.not_plotted_label == (
        "Nicht im Diagramm: 1 geplantes Projekt (AQ-118) und 1 abgeschlossenes."
    )

    assert kpi.risk_open_total == 4
    assert (kpi.risk_high, kpi.risk_medium, kpi.risk_low) == (2, 1, 1)
    assert kpi.risks[0].score == 20
    cells = {c.key: c.count for row in kpi.matrix for c in row.cells}
    assert cells["4-5"] == 1
    assert cells["3-3"] == 0
    assert kpi.matrix[0].probability == 5

    assert [p.code for p in kpi.chains] == ["AQ-104"]
    assert kpi.comfortable_label == (
        "Mit 4 Wochen Puffer oder mehr: AQ-112 +30. Ohne erfassten Bedarf: 1 Projekt."
    )
    assert kpi.gap_total == pytest.approx(30.0)

    kpi = portfolio.build_portfolio(_sample(), SCOPE_TEAM, TODAY)
    assert kpi.scope == "team"
    assert [p.code for p in kpi.projects] == ["AQ-104"]
    assert kpi.risk_open_total == 2


def test_build_portfolio_notices_and_unknown_scope() -> None:
    no_profile = replace(_sample(), current_employee_id=None)
    assert portfolio.build_portfolio(no_profile, SCOPE_TEAM, TODAY).notice == (
        portfolio.NO_PROFILE_NOTICE
    )
    lonely = replace(_sample(), current_employee_id=3)
    assert portfolio.build_portfolio(lonely, SCOPE_TEAM, TODAY).notice == (
        portfolio.EMPTY_TEAM_NOTICE
    )
    assert portfolio.build_portfolio(_sample(), "x", TODAY).scope == "department"

    )
    bubble = portfolio.bubbles([p])[0]
    assert bubble.label_left.startswith("calc(95% - ")
    assert portfolio.not_plotted_label([]) == ""

"""Minimal absence representation for utilization calculation."""

    start_date: date
    end_date: date


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HeatResult:
    """Utilization result for a single employee in a single week."""

    percent: int
    bucket: str
    is_absent: bool
    available_days: float
    used_days: float


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GesamtResult:
    """Free-days result for a single employee in a single week."""

    free_days: float
    bucket: str
    has_absence: bool


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProjectHeatResult:
    """Utilization result for a single project in a single week."""

    percent: int
        used_days: float,
        absence_days: float,
        internal_days: float,
        work_days: float = 5.0,
    ) -> HeatResult:
        """Compute heatmap percent for one employee in one week.

        This is the canonical formula used by the planning grid heatmap.
        Parameters use pre-computed values (internal already capped).
        """
        fully_absent = absence_days >= float(WORK_DAYS_PER_WEEK)
        available = max(0.0, work_days - internal_days - absence_days)

        if fully_absent:
            denom = work_days - internal_days
            pct = round((used_days / denom) * 100) if denom > 0 else 0
            bucket = "absent"
        elif available > 0:
            pct = round((used_days / available) * 100)
            bucket = cls.heat_bucket(pct)
        else:
            pct = 0
            bucket = "low"

        return HeatResult(
            percent=pct,
            bucket=bucket,
            is_absent=fully_absent,
            available_days=available,
            used_days=used_days,
        )

    @classmethod
    def compute_employee_gesamt(
        cls,
        used_days: float,
        absence_days: float,
        internal_days: float,
        work_days: float = 5.0,
    ) -> GesamtResult:
        """Compute free days for one employee in one week."""
        has_absence = absence_days > 0
        free = work_days - internal_days - used_days - absence_days
        bucket = "absent" if has_absence else cls.gesamt_bucket(free)
        return GesamtResult(free_days=free, bucket=bucket, has_absence=has_absence)

            bucket = "absent"
        elif available > 0:
            pct = round((used_days / available) * 100)
            bucket = cls.heat_bucket(pct)
        else:
            pct = 0
            bucket = "low"

        return HeatResult(
            percent=pct,
            bucket=bucket,
            is_absent=fully_absent,
            available_days=available,
            used_days=used_days,
        )

    @classmethod
    def compute_employee_gesamt(
        cls,
        used_days: float,
        absence_days: float,
        internal_days: float,
        work_days: float = 5.0,
    ) -> GesamtResult:
        """Compute free days for one employee in one week."""
        has_absence = absence_days > 0
        free = work_days - internal_days - used_days - absence_days
        bucket = "absent" if has_absence else cls.gesamt_bucket(free)
        return GesamtResult(free_days=free, bucket=bucket, has_absence=has_absence)

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

filePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a file to save the script output to. If omitted, the output is returned inline.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__fill_form
entries.description: Fill out multiple form elements (inputs, selects, checkboxes, radios) at once. ALWAYS prefer this tool over multiple individual 'fill' or 'click' calls when interacting with forms. It is significantly faster, more reliable, and reduces turn count. Example: Fill username, password, and check "Remember Me" in one call.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the element to fill out

value.description: Value for the element. "true" or "false" for checkboxes and toggles, "true" for radio buttons.

elements.description: Elements from snapshot to fill out.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__list_console_messages
entries.description: List all console messages for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of messages to return. When omitted, returns all messages.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

types.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all messages.

includePreservedMessages.description: Set to true to return the preserved messages over the last 3 navigations.

includeStackTraces.description: Set to true to include the stack trace for each message when available. Increases the response size.

serviceWorkerId.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified service worker.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__navigate_page
entries.description: Go to a URL, or back, forward, or reload. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

type.description: Navigate the page by URL, back or forward in history, or reload.

ignoreCache.description: Whether to ignore cache on reload.

handleBeforeUnload.description: Whether to auto accept or beforeunload dialogs triggered by this navigation. Default is accept.

initScript.description: A JavaScript script to be executed on each new document before any other scripts for the next navigation.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__new_page
entries.description: Open a new tab and load a URL. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

url.description: URL to load in a new page.

background.description: Whether to open the page in the background without bringing it to the front. Default is false (foreground).

isolatedContext.description: If specified, the page is created in an isolated browser context with the given name. Pages in the same browser context share cookies and storage. Pages in different browser contexts are fully isolated (useful for clean-slate testing of cookies and authentication).

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__press_key
entries.description: Press a key or key combination. Use this when other input methods like fill() cannot be used (e.g., keyboard shortcuts, navigation keys, or special key combinations).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

key.description: A key or a combination (e.g., "Enter", "Control+A", "Control++", "Control+Shift+R"). Modifiers: Control, Shift, Alt, Meta

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__take_screenshot
entries.description: Take a screenshot of the page or element.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

format.description: Type of format to save the screenshot as. Default is "png"

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP formats (0-100). Higher values mean better quality but larger file sizes. Ignored for PNG format.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot. If omitted, takes a page screenshot.

fullPage.description: If set to true takes a screenshot of the full page instead of the currently visible viewport. Incompatible with uid.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the screenshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__take_snapshot
entries.description:
Take a text snapshot of the target page based on the a11y tree. The snapshot lists page elements along with a unique
identifier (uid). Always use the latest snapshot. Prefer taking a snapshot over taking a screenshot. The snapshot indicates the element selected
in the DevTools Elements panel (if any).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

verbose.description: Whether to include all possible information available in the full a11y tree. Default is false.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the snapshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_jenreh-reflex_chrome-devtools__wait_for
entries.description: Wait for the specified text to appear on the selected page.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

text.description: Non-empty list of texts. Resolves when any value appears on the page.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.
